context_requirements: Expression of a class target with an activating or autocrine-dependent configuration: FLT3 (ITD or high wild-type), KIT, CSF1R, PDGFRA/B, or RET
RTK-addicted survival signalling through PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK and STAT5
Intact apoptotic machinery (no dominant anti-apoptotic block) for the 24 h death response
No dependence on ABCG2/ABCB1 efflux that would lower intracellular drug at 10 µM
falsifiers: No decrease in MYC, CCND1, or proliferation gene sets at 24 h in any line
No induction of immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN, DUSP6) at 6 h in any line
Strong, uniform transcriptional response across all nine lines, which would indicate a non-FLT3 off-target mechanism
Absence of any oxidative-stress or apoptosis signature at 24 h despite target expression

evidence.supports: FLT3 inhibition causes cell-cycle effects and apoptosis in FLT3/ITD-dependent leukemic cells
FLT3 inhibition alters central carbon metabolism, depletes glutathione and causes mitochondrial oxidative stress and apoptosis
FLT3/MERTK inhibition induces apoptosis and inhibits colony formation in AML cells
FLT3 inhibitors can interact with ABCB1/ABCG2 transporters, affecting intracellular drug levels

changes: Removed ETV1 from proximal_up: ETV1 is not a canonical immediate-early MAPK/ERK target gene and its direction under FLT3 inhibition is not justified by the cited evidence.

Changed all nine line_response values to 'none': none of the nine lines (A375, A549, HA1E, HCC515, HEPG2, HT29, MCF7, PC3, VCAP) are known to express an activating FLT3/CSF1R/KIT/PDGFRA/B/RET configuration or to be RTK-addicted to these targets, so a response cannot be justified.
Kept kinetics 'slow' and magnitude weak/moderate as consistent with indirect transcriptional consequences of RTK inhibition.
Kept evidence citations: all four abstracts support the stated claims about cell-cycle/apoptosis, oxidative stress, apoptosis induction, and ABC transporter interaction.
